title: DeFi is entering an interesting phase. We’re moving beyond simply giving people access to financial tools towards buildi
title_en:
DeFi is entering an interesting phase. We’re moving beyond simply giving people access to financial tools towards building systems that can actively help manage those tools.

The interesting part is what happens when Motes autonomous agents gain access to Aave’s lending infrastructure.

Aave has established itself as one of the leading names in decentralized lending and borrowing. Now, Motes is bringing another layer to that experience through AI agents capable of managing collateral, borrowing, repayments and monitoring health factors.

But there’s something even more important here.

Motes Genesis NFTs give users dedicated AI agents with personalized strategies and user-defined permissions.

Think about that: an AI agent that can help manage your DeFi positions, monitor risk and execute permitted actions without giving up control of the rules.

That’s a meaningful shift in how people could interact with decentralized finance.

The future of DeFi may not just be about having more financial tools. It could be about having intelligent agents that know how to use them within the limits you set.

Interesting times ahead for @meetmotes

有趣的是，当 Motes 自治代理访问 Aave 的借贷基础设施时会发生什么。

Aave 已成为去中心化借贷领域的领先品牌

title:
not every opportunity in defi needs to be a trade.

sometimes, putting capital to work through lending can make more sen
title_en:
not every opportunity in defi needs to be a trade.

sometimes, putting capital to work through lending can make more sense than taking another market position.

that's one thing i want to understand better about the @meetmotes and @aave integration.

imagine an AI agent managing a user's capital. it may find a trading opportunity, but it could also identify a lending opportunity where the capital isn't currently being used.

now the decision becomes more than simply finding the next trade.

how should the agent compare potential trading returns with lending yields? how much liquidity should it keep available? and when should it avoid deploying capital altogether?

these decisions involve different risks, time horizons, and liquidity requirements.

i think this is where autonomous capital management becomes more meaningful.

the goal shouldn't be to keep every dollar constantly active. it should be to understand where capital makes the most sense at a given moment.

sometimes the best financial decision isn't making another move. it's choosing where your capital should wait.

title:
Happy weekend guys 
When an AI agent starts spending money for someone, it becomes more than a chatbot, basically an eco
title_en:
Happy weekend guys 
When an AI agent starts spending money for someone, it becomes more than a chatbot, basically an economic actor

and thats where the real questions start

Who takes responsibility when an agent picks the wrong service, misunderstands a brief or pays for something that turns out useless?

Giving agents tools is easy. making different agents work together, exchange value and deal with problems is a much harder thing

Thats why @termix_ai caught my attention

Its SDK lets developers connect agent services directly into existing apps, with service discovery, orders, onchain settlement, escrow, revisions and dispute flows

so you dont need to build a whole marketplace just to let users access external agents

But connecting them isnt enough. agents need boundaries too. what can they buy, how much can they spend and what happens when the result doesnt match the agreement?

Without those limits, automation can make bad decisions at scale

Think of booking a trip. one agent finds flights, another handles hotels, another checks local services. all working in the background while you just use one app

thats a pretty interesting direction for software

The real challenge isnt making agents more autonomous, its letting them act without losing control over permissions, payments and accountability

and I think thats where infrastructure like TermiX becomes much more important

so you dont need to build a whole marketplace just to let users access external agents

But connecting them isnt enough. agents need boundaries too. what can they buy, how much can they spend and what happens when the result doesnt match the agreement?

full_text_zh:
周末快乐各位
当人工智能代理开始为某人花钱时，它就不仅仅是一个聊天机器人，基本上是一个经济参与者

这就是真正的问题开始的地方

当代理人选择了错误的服务、误解了简报或为无用的东西付费时，谁该承担责任？

为代理提供工具很容易。让不同的智能体协同工作、交换价值、处理问题是一件更困难的事情

这就是为什么@termix_ai 引起了我的注意

其 SDK 允许开发人员将代理服务直接连接到现有应用程序中，包括服务发现、订单、链上结算、托管、修订和争议流

因此您不需要仅仅为了让用户访问外部代理而构建整个市场

但将它们连接起来还不够。代理人也需要边界。他们可以购买什么、可以花多少钱以及当结果与协议不符时会发生什么？

如果没有这些限制，自动化可能会大规模做出错误的决策

考虑预订一次旅行。一名代理人查找航班，另一名代理人处理酒店，另一名代理人检查当地服务。当您只使用一个应用程序时，所有这些都在后台工作

这对于软件来说是一个非常有趣的方向

真正的挑战不是让代理人更加自主，而是让他们在不失去对权限、付款和责任的控制的情况下采取行动

我认为这就是像 TermiX 这样的基础设施变得更加重要的地方

→ 爱马仕代理：45% → 61%
→ 开放代码：47% → 67%
→ 圆周率：74% → 74%

title: What if your profile picture was not just an NFT to display, but the identity of an AI agent you could actually control
title_en:
What if your profile picture was not just an NFT to display, but the identity of an AI agent you could actually control That is the concept behind

@meetmotes starts with its Genesis NFT collection, marked as coming soon, but the bigger idea 

goes beyond digital artwork. Each of the 20,000 Motes is designed to represent one agent identity, with the NFT acting as its public face and ownership reference

Here is how the structure connects:
One NFT represents one agent identity.

That identity is linked to its own smart account.

The owner funds the account with USDC and signs the permissions that govern the agent.

Those permissions define what the agent can trade, how much capital it can use, and when it must stop

The agent can only propose actions within the owner’s approved policy. Motes describes the policy as including valid targets, assets, 

limits, and an expiry window, while the account validates the signer and owner policy before execution.

title: John von Neumann helped invent the modern computer, and he got furious when one of his grad students made programming ea
title_en:
John von Neumann helped invent the modern computer, and he got furious when one of his grad students made programming easier.

The student, Don Gillies, was stuck hand-translating programs into binary for von Neumann's machine at Princeton. So he wrote a program to do the translating for him, which he later said was the first assembler. Von Neumann told him you don't use a valuable scientific computing instrument for clerical work.

And honestly, for the early 1950s he had a point. The machine was the precious thing back then, and a grad student's afternoon was close to free.

That math flipped fast. John Backus, who led the FORTRAN team at IBM, later wrote that by 1954 a computer center's programmers usually cost at least as much as the computer itself, and a quarter to half of the machine's time went to debugging their code. Human time had become the thing worth saving.

So Backus's team built a language where you write something close to algebra and the machine writes the code. A lot of experienced programmers hated it. Backus said many of them saw themselves as "members of a priesthood," guarding skills too complex for ordinary people. He also wrote that they rightly saw their work as a creative art, and he took that seriously. His team was convinced FORTRAN would never catch on unless its programs came out almost as efficient as hand-coded ones, so that's where most of their effort went. Once it delivered, people could stop worrying about the machine code underneath. Most programmers working today have never read the assembly their code turns into.

That's the question this video is asking. What was every programming language reaching for?

Karpathy, who's at Anthropic now, posted in January that he's "mostly programming in English now" and admitted it hurts the ego a bit. In Sonar's new survey, developers say AI writes or heavily assists about 65% of the code they commit, up from 42% a year ago.

So we're back in 1957, fighting over whether you can trust what the machine wrote without reading it. Only 45% of those developers think AI code is even functionally correct, and the share who say they always check it before committing still dropped from 48% to 39% in a year. 76% admit they generate AI code faster than they can verify it.

That's where the old-school programmer comes back in. By this summer, software job postings on Indeed were up almost 15% since Claude Code launched, while postings overall fell 7%. 71% of that rebound went to senior roles, mostly people who know the new tools too. Knowing what's actually happening underneath, the same skill the priesthood guarded, is what checking all that code takes.

Grace Hopper had the answer in the 1950s. She wanted people to write programs in plain English, and she was told computers didn't understand English. She died in 1992, about 30 years before they did.

full_text_zh:
约翰·冯·诺依曼帮助发明了现代计算机，当他的一名研究生让编程变得更容易时，他感到非常愤怒。

学生唐·吉利斯 (Don Gillies) 在普林斯顿大学的冯·诺依曼机器上手工将程序翻译成二进制。因此，他编写了一个程序来为他进行翻译，他后来说这是第一个汇编程序。冯·诺依曼告诉他，你不会使用有价值的科学计算仪器来进行文书工作。

老实说，在 20 世纪 50 年代初，他说得有道理。那时机器是很珍贵的东西，研究生的下午几乎是空闲的。

数学翻转得很快。 IBM FORTRAN 团队的领导者 John Backus 后来写道，到 1954 年，计算机中心的程序员的成本通常至少与计算机本身一样高，并且机器四分之一到一半的时间都花在了调试代码上。人类的时间已经成为值得拯救的东西。

因此，巴科斯的团队构建了一种语言，您可以在其中编写接近代数的内容，然后由机器编写代码。许多经验丰富的程序员讨厌它。巴克斯说，他们中的许多人将自己视为“神职人员”，守护技能对于普通人来说过于复杂。他还写道，他们正确地将自己的作品视为一种创造性艺术，他认真对待这一点。他的团队确信 FORTRAN 永远不会流行起来，除非它的程序几乎和手工编码的程序一样高效，所以这就是他们大部分努力的方向。一旦交付，人们就可以不再担心底层的机器代码。今天工作的大多数程序员从未阅读过他们的代码变成的程序集。

这就是这个视频要问的问题。每种编程语言的目标是什么？

现在在 Anthropic 工作的 Karpathy 一月份发帖称，他“现在主要用英语编程”，并承认这有点伤害自尊。在 Sonar 的新调查中，开发人员表示，他们提交的代码中约有 65% 由人工智能编写或大力协助，高于一年前的 42%。

所以我们回到了 1957 年，争论是否可以在不阅读机器所写内容的情况下相信它。只有 45% 的开发人员认为 AI 代码在功能上是正确的，而表示在提交之前总是进行检查的开发人员比例在一年内仍然从 48% 下降到 39%。 76% 的人承认他们生成人工智能代码的速度比验证代码的速度快。

这就是老派程序员回归的地方。到今年夏天，自 Claude Code 推出以来，Indeed 上的软件职位发布量增加了近 15%，而总体职位发布量下降了 7%。 71% 的反弹流向了高级职位，其中大多数人也了解新工具。知道底层实际发生了什么，这与祭司所守护的技能相同，也是检查所有代码所需要的。

格蕾丝·霍珀 (Grace Hopper) 在 20 世纪 50 年代找到了答案。她希望人们用简单的英语编写程序，但她被告知计算机听不懂英语。她于 1992 年去世，比他们早了大约 30 年。

title_en:
This Anthropic harness paper is f*cking gold

Anthropic's Labs team handed Claude one sentence and got a full app back 6 hours later. And the model wasn't the upgrade.

The upgrade: three agents, and none of them grades its own work.

prompt → spec → contract → build → QA → fix

The 6 parts of the harness:

Part 1 → planner

1-4 sentences in, a 16-feature spec out.
Product level only, no implementation details.

Part 2 → sprint contract

Before any code, the generator and the evaluator agree on "done".
In files, back and forth.

Part 3 → generator

One feature per sprint.
Self-check, then hand off to QA.

Part 4 → evaluator

Clicks through the running app with Playwright.
Sprint 3 alone had 27 criteria.

Part 5 → hard thresholds

Depth, functionality, design, code.
One score under the bar → the sprint fails.

Part 6 → cost

Solo: 20 min, $9, the game ignored input.
Harness: 6 hr, $200, the game was playable.

An agent that grades itself always passes. A stranger with Playwright doesn't.

I packed all 6 parts into one prompt. Drop it into Claude Code and it sets the harness up for you.

3 agents. 1 prompt. 0 self-grading.

Then read the article below ↓

title:
🚨 Your "deleted" photos might not be deleted.

Claude Code just found years of them hiding in a cache on my iPhone.

It
title_en:
🚨 Your "deleted" photos might not be deleted.

Claude Code just found years of them hiding in a cache on my iPhone.

It started as a routine backup. I plugged my iPhone into my MacBook, and while it ran, I had Claude Code do a quick security check. It flagged something I wasn't even looking for: a directory called PhotoData/Thumbnails.

Inside were thousands of files. Photos, videos, screenshots. And a lot of them were things I had deleted.

Pictures from a couple of years ago. Screenshots I'd snapped and trashed seconds later. Even items I had cleared out of Recently Deleted. Some were still sitting right there.

Here's a sample of what I found:

→ Old screenshots of banking apps
→ Photos I deleted right after taking them
→ Random shots I never wanted on my phone
→ A few things I clearly remember deleting more than once

Here's what's going on. When you delete a photo, iOS removes it from your camera roll and from Recently Deleted. But it keeps a compressed copy in a Spotlight search cache, so your phone can still find things when you search. And that cache doesn't get fully cleared.

So I checked which apps had Files and Folders access. There were more than I expected, including apps I'd downloaded ages ago and completely forgotten about. Any of them could potentially read files from that cache.

I went through the list and revoked access for most of them.

The prompt I used is below. If you already have a backup, it takes just a few minutes.

Now I'm curious: how many apps on your phone have Files access right now?

full_text_zh:
🚨 您“已删除”的照片可能不会被删除。

Claude Code 刚刚在我 iPhone 的缓存中发现了多年的秘密。

它最初是作为例行备份。我将 iPhone 插入 MacBook，当它运行时，我让 Claude Code 进行快速安全检查。它标记了一些我根本没有寻找的东西：一个名为 PhotoData/Thumbnails 的目录。

里面有数千个文件。照片、视频、屏幕截图。其中很多都是我删除的。

几年前的照片。我拍下的屏幕截图几秒钟后就被扔掉了。即使是我从“最近删除”中清除的项目。有些人还坐在那儿。

这是我发现的示例：

→ 银行应用程序的旧屏幕截图
→ 照片拍完后立即删除
→ 我从来不想在手机上随机拍摄
→ 有几件事我清楚地记得不止一次删除过

这是发生的事情。当您删除照片时，iOS 会将其从相机胶卷和“最近删除”中删除。但它会在 Spotlight 搜索缓存中保留压缩副本，因此您的手机在搜索时仍然可以找到内容。并且该缓存没有被完全清除。

因此，我检查了哪些应用程序具有文件和文件夹访问权限。其中的内容超出了我的预期，其中包括我很久以前下载并完全忘记的应用程序。他们中的任何一个都可能从该缓存中读取文件。

我浏览了该列表并撤销了其中大多数人的访问权限。

我使用的提示如下。如果您已经有备份，则只需几分钟。

现在我很好奇：您手机上有多少应用程序现在可以访问文件？

title:
One Ledger, Two Very Different Industries — How Does That Work?

Actum's PoHA runs in production in two completely diffe
title_en:
One Ledger, Two Very Different Industries — How Does That Work?

Actum's PoHA runs in production in two completely different settings: a rail transit equipment manufacturer, with 5,000+ machines and operators doing hourly inspections; and a commercial hospitality setting, with guest data and service records flowing back and forth.

What the two settings need looks nothing alike — the factory needs every bolt's inspection tied to a person; the hotel needs every data access traceable. But underneath, the problem is the same: when an action happens, who was there, who authorized it, can you trace it afterward, can you hold someone accountable?

PoHA's answer is one shared ledger: Humans, Machines, and AI Agents, verified against the same standard, speaking through the same evidence. A pre-frozen codebook before the action, six-dimensional verification at the gate, signed attestation after — a factory inspection check-in and a hotel data access go through the same process.

The numbers: the ledger now produces ~5,800 verified events a day across 5,300+ endpoints, with 174,000+ on-chain attestations in the past 30 days, 0 failures, 99.986% coverage.

Different industries, same ledger. That's why PoHA can move from one setting to another: it doesn't solve one industry's business problem. It solves the problem every industry shares — who is accountable for what AI does.

full_text_en:
One Ledger, Two Very Different Industries — How Does That Work?

Actum's PoHA runs in production in two completely different settings: a rail transit equipment manufacturer, with 5,000+ machines and operators doing hourly inspections; and a commercial hospitality setting, with guest data and service records flowing back and forth.

What the two settings need looks nothing alike — the factory needs every bolt's inspection tied to a person; the hotel needs every data access traceable. But underneath, the problem is the same: when an action happens, who was there, who authorized it, can you trace it afterward, can you hold someone accountable?

PoHA's answer is one shared ledger: Humans, Machines, and AI Agents, verified against the same standard, speaking through the same evidence. A pre-frozen codebook before the action, six-dimensional verification at the gate, signed attestation after — a factory inspection check-in and a hotel data access go through the same process.

The numbers: the ledger now produces ~5,800 verified events a day across 5,300+ endpoints, with 174,000+ on-chain attestations in the past 30 days, 0 failures, 99.986% coverage.

Different industries, same ledger. That's why PoHA can move from one setting to another: it doesn't solve one industry's business problem. It solves the problem every industry shares — who is accountable for what AI does.
full_text_zh:
一个账本，两个截然不同的行业——这是如何运作的？

Actum 的 PoHA 在两种完全不同的环境中运行：轨道交通设备制造商，拥有 5,000 多台机器和操作员每小时进行检查；以及商业接待环境，客人数据和服务记录来回流动。

这两种设置所需要的东西看起来一点都不像——工厂需要每个螺栓的检查都由专人负责；酒店需要每一次数据访问都可追溯。但本质上，问题是相同的：当某个行为发生时，谁在场，谁授权了它，事后你能追踪它吗？你能追究某人的责任吗？

PoHA 的答案是一个共享账本：人类、机器和人工智能代理，根据相同的标准进行验证，通过相同的证据进行阐述。行动前预冻密码本，门口六维验证，行动后签名鉴证——工厂检查签到和酒店数据访问都是同一流程。

数字：账本现在每天在 5,300 多个端点上生成约 5,800 个经过验证的事件，过去 30 天内有 174,000 多个链上证明，0 次失败，覆盖率 99.986%。

不同的行业，相同的账本。这就是 PoHA 可以从一种环境转移到另一种环境的原因：它不能解决一个行业的业务问题。它解决了每个行业都面临的问题——谁对人工智能的工作负责。

title: Two days ago, we published our report on Anthropic’s IPO, drawing on research involving more than 80 enterprise customer
title_en:
Two days ago, we published our report on Anthropic’s IPO, drawing on research involving more than 80 enterprise customers. One interesting finding is that enterprise adoption may be slower than the market expects, particularly between now and the end of the first half of next year. Adoption could start to accelerate around the middle of next year.

The 58 traditional enterprises we track generally expect AI spending growth to slow in 2027. A closer look at their spending mix and project pipelines suggests that growth is shifting from paid seats to more complex applications, rather than demand reaching a ceiling.

On average, respondents expect AI spending to rise about 31% year over year in 2027. Roughly 60% expect slower growth next year than this year, and a small number expect spending to be flat or decline.

Report https://t.co/AbvYqmMm41
title_zh:

full_text_zh:
两天前，我们根据对 80 多家企业客户的研究，发布了有关 Anthropic IPO 的报告。一个有趣的发现是，企业采用可能比市场预期慢，特别是从现在到明年上半年末。明年年中左右，采用可能会开始加速。

我们跟踪的 58 家传统企业普遍预计 2027 年人工智能支出增长将放缓。仔细观察他们的支出结构和项目管道表明，增长正在从付费席位转向更复杂的应用程序，而不是需求达到上限。

平均而言，受访者预计 2027 年人工智能支出将同比增长约 31%。大约 60% 的受访者预计明年的增长速度将低于今年，少数人预计支出将持平或下降。

title: Giving an AI agent access to capital is one thing. Giving it a defined budget, a limited session and a clear strategy to
title_en:
Giving an AI agent access to capital is one thing. Giving it a defined budget, a limited session and a clear strategy to follow is another.

I was looking into @termix_ai’s BNB Chain Quant Agent, and the structure stood out. Users choose a trading strategy, set a capital limit and a time period, then let the agent operate through a wallet created specifically for that job. The session can be revoked at any time.

What I find interesting is how the roles are separated: one side provides the capital, another provides the strategy, and the agent handles execution within the assigned limits.

That lets strategy providers and capital owners work together without handing an agent unlimited access to funds.

I think that’s a more practical direction for agent-based DeFi than fully open-ended autonomy.

But limits protect against runaway access, not against a bad strategy. The real question is how these strategies perform over time, not just how easily an agent can execute trades.

Would you let an agent trade with your capital under a strict limit, and what would you want to see first?

full_text_en:
Giving an AI agent access to capital is one thing. Giving it a defined budget, a limited session and a clear strategy to follow is another.

I was looking into @termix_ai’s BNB Chain Quant Agent, and the structure stood out. Users choose a trading strategy, set a capital limit and a time period, then let the agent operate through a wallet created specifically for that job. The session can be revoked at any time.

What I find interesting is how the roles are separated: one side provides the capital, another provides the strategy, and the agent handles execution within the assigned limits.

That lets strategy providers and capital owners work together without handing an agent unlimited access to funds.

I think that’s a more practical direction for agent-based DeFi than fully open-ended autonomy.

But limits protect against runaway access, not against a bad strategy. The real question is how these strategies perform over time, not just how easily an agent can execute trades.

Would you let an agent trade with your capital under a strict limit, and what would you want to see first?
full_text_zh:
让人工智能代理获得资本是一回事。另一件事是给它一个明确的预算、有限的会议时间和明确的遵循策略。

我正在研究 @termix_ai 的 BNB Chain Quant Agent，其结构很突出。用户选择交易策略，设置资金限额和时间段，然后让代理通过专门为该工作创建的钱包进行操作。该会话可以随时撤销。

我发现有趣的是角色是如何分离的：一侧提供资本，另一侧提供策略，代理在指定的限制内处理执行。

这使得策略提供者和资本所有者可以合作，而无需让代理人无限制地获取资金。

我认为对于基于代理的 DeFi 来说，这是比完全开放式自治更实用的方向。

但限制可以防止失控的访问，而不是防止糟糕的策略。真正的问题是这些策略如何随着时间的推移而发挥作用，而不仅仅是代理执行交易的容易程度。

你会让代理人在严格的限制下用你的资金进行交易吗？你希望首先看到什么？

title:
Same agent ID. Different model. Same reputation?

Here's an interesting problem I've been thinking about while exploring
title_en:
Same agent ID. Different model. Same reputation?

Here's an interesting problem I've been thinking about while exploring @termix_ai and ERC-8004.

Imagine an AI agent that has completed 500 jobs with a 98% success rate.

Pretty solid track record, right?

Now imagine its developer replaces the underlying model, changes its tools and completely rewrites how it executes tasks.

The agent still has the same onchain identity.

But is it really the same agent you trusted yesterday?

This is where AI agent versioning gets interesting.

ERC-8004 provides a framework for persistent agent identities and reputation signals, but an identity alone doesn't tell you whether the software behind it has changed.

And that's a pretty important distinction.

I think future agent marketplaces should make it easier to track:

❯ Model versions and major updates
❯ Changes to tools and execution environments
❯ Performance before and after upgrades
❯ Which version actually completed each job

This matters for something like TermiX's AACP, where agents can provide services, build reputation and participate in onchain transactions.

A reputation score earned by version 1.0 shouldn't automatically guarantee that version 2.0 performs just as well.

Of course, updates can make agents significantly better.

The point isn't to discourage upgrades.

It's to make sure reputation reflects what an agent can actually deliver today, not just what an older version achieved months ago.

Because a persistent identity is valuable.

But a verifiable history of what changed behind that identity could be even more useful.

full_text_zh:
相同的代理 ID。不同型号。一样的名气吗？

这是我在探索 @termix_ai 和 ERC-8004 时一直在思考的一个有趣的问题。

想象一下，一个 AI 代理已经完成了 500 项工作，成功率高达 98%。

相当可靠的记录，对吧？

现在想象一下，它的开发人员替换了底层模型，更改了其工具并完全重写了其执行任务的方式。

代理仍然具有相同的链上身份。

但这真的是你昨天信任的那个代理人吗？

这就是人工智能代理版本控制变得有趣的地方。

ERC-8004 提供了持久代理身份和声誉信号的框架，但身份本身并不能告诉您其背后的软件是否已更改。

这是一个非常重要的区别。

我认为未来的代理市场应该更容易追踪：

❯ 型号版本及主要更新
❯ 工具和执行环境的变化
❯ 升级前后的性能
❯ 哪个版本实际完成了每项工作

这对于像 TermiX 的 AACP 这样的东西很重要，代理可以在其中提供服务、建立声誉并参与链上交易。

版本 1.0 获得的声誉分数不应自动保证版本 2.0 的性能同样好。

当然，更新可以使代理变得更好。

重点不是阻止升级。

这是为了确保声誉反映代理今天实际可以交付的内容，而不仅仅是旧版本几个月前取得的成果。

因为持久的身份是有价值的。

但了解该身份背后发生的变化的可验证历史可能会更有用。

title:
How to increase Qwen3.8-27B inference speed from 25 tok/s to 91 tok/s for free on the same GPU?

The authors of the infe
title_en:
How to increase Qwen3.8-27B inference speed from 25 tok/s to 91 tok/s for free on the same GPU?

The authors of the inference-optimisation-skill project demonstrated this using the Intel Arc Pro B70 and Qwen3.8-27B as an example:

- llama.cpp Q4_K_M: 25 tok/s
- vLLM EXL3 4 bpw with custom kernels: 91.2 tok/s

They also created an open-source skill that allows an AI agent to independently search for ways to optimize local models.

How does it work?

- calculates the theoretical hardware performance limit
- analyzes what limits the model's speed
- changes one parameter and runs a benchmark
- Compares the results with control measurements
- rejects changes that degrade stability or performance with long context

Results on RTX 3090 with Qwen3.8-27B in EXL3 3 bpw and MTP:
- Prose: 96.2 tok/s
- Code: 141.1 tok/s

This is not another inference engine, but an optimization methodology that can be passed to an AI agent.

Would you let an AI agent optimize the configuration of your local LLM all night long?

title:
There are 3 ways to use AI effectively.

1. Automation

You know exactly what you want to achieve. You give AI clear ins
title_en:
There are 3 ways to use AI effectively.

1. Automation

You know exactly what you want to achieve. You give AI clear instructions, and it handles the task for you.

2. Augmentation

You’re still figuring things out. You use AI to brainstorm, explore ideas, solve problems and think through possibilities. You and AI work together.

3. Agency

You give AI a goal, the necessary knowledge and responsibilities, and it works independently on your behalf.

For example, an AI agent that handles customer enquiries 24/7 without you having to respond to every message manually.

Automation gets things done. Augmentation helps you think better. Agency gives AI the ability to act independently.

Learning when and how to use all three is where the real advantage lies.

title: ‼️ UPDATE: The hackers who planted malware in Microsoft's AI agent toolkit on PyPI pushed it through Microsoft's own rel
title_en:
‼️ UPDATE: The hackers who planted malware in Microsoft's AI agent toolkit on PyPI pushed it through Microsoft's own release system, with a stolen Microsoft certificate and private key.

Cloud security firm Wiz says their first try, from AWS, was blocked. The second, from a Microsoft-owned network, went through.

How the key was stolen is not yet known. Wiz counted three confirmed thefts of victim data before both versions were pulled within the hour.

The attackers' own AI hacking tool gave part of the operation away, reporting its progress to the same web address the stolen data went to.

title:
I think there’s a major misunderstanding in this discussion.

The growing number of vulnerabilities discovered in open s
title_en:
I think there’s a major misunderstanding in this discussion.

The growing number of vulnerabilities discovered in open source software doesn’t necessarily mean that open source code is worse than proprietary software.

What we’re seeing is a massive increase in scrutiny.

For years, many open source projects simply didn’t receive thorough security reviews. Nobody had the time, resources or financial incentive to look that closely.

Now anyone with access to a capable LLM can point it at a public repository and start looking for vulnerabilities. And newer models are getting remarkably good at finding issues that previous tools and human reviewers missed.

But something very similar is happening behind closed doors.

I can tell you from our own experience, and from discussions with people at other software companies, that internal development teams are also struggling with a flood of findings from AI-assisted code reviews.

Many of these findings concern code that has been running in production for years. In proprietary software development, they rarely become public CVEs or security advisories. They end up as Jira tickets, creating backlogs that take weeks or months to process.

Ironically, while AI accelerates software development, it’s also slowing teams down by exposing years of accumulated technical debt and security issues that nobody had identified before.

So I’d be careful about interpreting the current wave of open source vulnerabilities as evidence of lower code quality.
title_zh:
我认为这次讨论存在重大误解。

开源软件中发现的漏洞数量不断增加并不一定意味着开源代码比专有软件更糟糕。

我们看到的是审查的大幅增加。

多年来，许多开源项目根本没有接受彻底的安全审查。没有人有时间、资源或经济动力来仔细观察。

现在，任
full_text_en:
I think there’s a major misunderstanding in this discussion.

The growing number of vulnerabilities discovered in open source software doesn’t necessarily mean that open source code is worse than proprietary software.

What we’re seeing is a massive increase in scrutiny.

For years, many open source projects simply didn’t receive thorough security reviews. Nobody had the time, resources or financial incentive to look that closely.

Now anyone with access to a capable LLM can point it at a public repository and start looking for vulnerabilities. And newer models are getting remarkably good at finding issues that previous tools and human reviewers missed.

But something very similar is happening behind closed doors.

I can tell you from our own experience, and from discussions with people at other software companies, that internal development teams are also struggling with a flood of findings from AI-assisted code reviews.

Many of these findings concern code that has been running in production for years. In proprietary software development, they rarely become public CVEs or security advisories. They end up as Jira tickets, creating backlogs that take weeks or months to process.

Ironically, while AI accelerates software development, it’s also slowing teams down by exposing years of accumulated technical debt and security issues that nobody had identified before.

So I’d be careful about interpreting the current wave of open source vulnerabilities as evidence of lower code quality.
full_text_zh:
我认为这次讨论存在重大误解。

开源软件中发现的漏洞数量不断增加并不一定意味着开源代码比专有软件更糟糕。

我们看到的是审查的大幅增加。

多年来，许多开源项目根本没有接受彻底的安全审查。没有人有时间、资源或经济动力来仔细观察。

现在，任何有权访问有能力的法学硕士的人都可以将其指向公共存储库并开始寻找漏洞。较新的模型非常擅长发现以前的工具和人工审核人员遗漏的问题。

但非常相似的事情正在幕后发生。

我可以根据我们自己的经验以及与其他软件公司人员的讨论告诉您，内部开发团队也在努力应对人工智能辅助代码审查的大量发现。

其中许多发现涉及已在生产环境中运行多年的代码。在专有软件开发中，它们很少成为公共 CVE 或安全公告。它们最终会成为 Jira 票证，造成积压，需要数周或数月的时间才能处理。

具有讽刺意味的是，虽然人工智能加速了软件开发，但它也暴露了多年来积累的技术债务和以前没有人发现的安全问题，从而减慢了团队的速度。

因此，我会谨慎地将当前的开源漏洞浪潮解释为代码质量较低的证据。

title:
Opening A Position Is Easy, Managing It Is Where Things Get Complicated.

Anyone who has used lending protocols knows th
title_en:
Opening A Position Is Easy, Managing It Is Where Things Get Complicated.

Anyone who has used lending protocols knows the position doesn't manage itself.

You have to keep track of collateral, monitor your Health Factor, understand how much borrowing room remains and react when market conditions change.

That ongoing responsibility is one of the more interesting problems AI agents could help address.

@meetmotes has now integrated with @aave, extending its agents into decentralised lending and borrowing.

The integration introduces capabilities around:

➠ Collateral management: Helping manage collateral as lending positions evolve.

➠ Borrowing and repayment: Automating parts of the borrowing process and repayment.

➠ Health Factor monitoring: Tracking position health and applying automated risk controls.

What makes this particularly relevant to Motes is the connection to Genesis NFTs. 

Each Genesis NFT is designed to link its owner to a dedicated AI Agent, with personalised DeFi strategies operating within permissions defined by the owner.

I think risk management deserves just as much attention as execution when evaluating autonomous finance.

An agent that can open positions is useful. One designed to monitor collateral, track liquidation risk and operate within clear limits addresses a much bigger part of the problem.

With Aave joining its integrations, Motes is expanding the financial activities its agents are designed to handle.

The goal is becoming clearer: autonomous execution with owner-defined control.

这种持续的责任是人工智能代理可以帮助解决的更有趣的问题之一。

开仓很容易，管理仓位却变得复杂。

任何使用过借贷协议的人都知道，这个头寸无法自行管理。

您必须跟踪抵押品，监控您的健康因素，了解剩余的借贷空间，并在市场状况变化时做出反应。

这种持续的责任是人工智能代理可以帮助解决的更有趣的问题之一。

@meetmotes 现已与 @aave 整合，将其代理扩展到去中心化借贷领域。

➠ 抵押品管理：随着贷款头寸的变化帮助管理抵押品。

➠ 健康因素监控：跟踪职位健康状况并应用自动化风险控制。

这与 Motes 特别相关的是与 Genesis NFT 的联系。

每个 Genesis NFT 都旨在将其所有者与专用 AI 代理联系起来，并在所有者定义的权限内运行个性化的 DeFi 策略。

我认为在评估自主财务时，风险管理与执行同样值得关注。

可以开仓的代理很有用。旨在监控抵押品、跟踪清算风险并在明确限制内运作的方案可以解决更大的问题。

随着 Aave 加入其整合，Motes 正在扩大其代理旨在处理的金融活动。

目标变得越来越清晰：通过所有者定义的控制进行自主执行。

title_en:
An AI agent becomes much more interesting when it can move beyond having an identity and actually put that identity to work.

That's what caught my attention about the latest update from @termix_ai .

With Binance Agent ID support and TermiX Skills, agents can now connect with supported marketplace workflows on https://t.co/VuAqJW4igb.

This opens up some interesting possibilities:

- Discover available jobs and services.
- Work with other specialized agents.
- Complete tasks and receive payments.
- Build a reputation through real marketplace activity.

There's also a nice incentive for Binance Agent ID holders. Connect your linked agent's Agentic Wallet during Skills installation and receive 50 TermiX Points, subject to the eligibility rules.

Another interesting part is the ongoing exploration through the @BinanceWallet and @BNBCHAIN Agent ID Hackathon.

I think the real opportunity here goes beyond giving AI agents unique identities.

It's about creating an environment where they can find work, collaborate, deliver results and build trust through actual activity.

Still early, but this is definitely an area worth watching.

Explore: https://t.co/LHCc8O3iOz

title:
Reposting this 👇  

Danish municipalities are actively blocking citizens from seeing the real numbers on untreated sewag
title_en:
Reposting this 👇  

Danish municipalities are actively blocking citizens from seeing the real numbers on untreated sewage dumped into our fjords and the sea.

When one guy simply asks for the data under the law, Jammerbugt Kommune:
❌ illegally demands MitID  
❌ accuses him of being an “AI agent” who wants to harm the country  
❌ gives him a fake email so the complaint never arrives  

And this is not a one-off.

13+ freedom-of-information requests show the same pattern everywhere:
• Almost no physical flow meters — just computer models with 50-135% uncertainty  
• Known errors (up to 11x wrong) are locked into the official water plans on purpose  
• The Environmental Agency admits it does NOT enforce the difference between model and reality  
• Illegal discharges without permits, forgotten police reports, blacked-out pages  

Meanwhile the same system is crushing Danish farmers with nitrogen rules based on those exact models.

When the people responsible for our water refuse to measure their own sewage, block the data, and call transparency “harmful to the country” — that says everything.

This is about drinking water.  
This is about basic competence.  
The hole is getting bigger. 

The number of people who have failed us is enormous. 🚨

title:
Your AI Agent Can Place the Order. But Can It Prove You're Old Enough?

🧵 1/5

Imagine asking your AI assistant to order
title_en:
Your AI Agent Can Place the Order. But Can It Prove You're Old Enough?

🧵 1/5

Imagine asking your AI assistant to order a bottle of wine for you while you're busy doing something else.

It finds the product, checks the price, adds it to your basket and prepares to complete the purchase.

Then the shop asks one question: is the person making this purchase over 18?

The agent can process the order, but it cannot simply assume that its owner meets the requirement. And sending your passport to every service the agent interacts with would create an entirely different privacy problem.

This is where verified identity becomes important in the agentic economy.

title_en:
India is becoming Microsoft’s largest infrastructure bet globally. 💰
$20B+ committed. 4 data centre regions. Subsea cables wiring Southeast Asia. 🌊〰️🌐

The centre of gravity for global AI compute is shifting. 📍

As Judson Althoff (CEO, Microsoft Commercial Business) put it: “There’s no more important market than India for Microsoft”, serving India from India, and enabling India to serve more of the world.

What’s being built under the hood:
• 60–70% Cheaper AI: Building an end-to-end stack: in-house frontier models (MAI), cloud infra & custom silicon, to slash enterprise AI execution costs while protecting proprietary data.

• Tailwind for Indian IT: Microsoft’s new $2.5B “Frontier Company” unit (6,000 forward-deployed engineers) won’t compete head-on with Indian IT, it acts as a demand stimulator, relying on partners to scale execution.

• Multi-Model Play: Reducing single-lab concentration while continuing partnerships with OpenAI and Meta.

India is no longer just an AI services back office.
It is becoming the compute, subsea, and enterprise deployment hub for the region.

title_en:
Giving an AI agent the ability to execute a task is not the same as knowing whether that task was executed correctly.

That distinction is becoming increasingly important.

As autonomous systems gain access to business tools, industrial processes, and sensitive workflows, the consequences of their actions become more significant.

Simply trusting that an agent followed instructions is not a sustainable approach.

Organizations need visibility into behavior, evidence of execution, and ways to verify what happened.

This is the bigger opportunity behind behavioral verification.

. @Actum_system is working to address this need through infrastructure designed for real-world AI operations.

I find this direction particularly interesting because it focuses on a problem that becomes more important as AI capabilities expand.

The future shouldn’t be autonomous systems acting without oversight.

It should be autonomous systems operating with verifiable accountability.

title:
I came across an interesting finding in yesterday’s @databricks announcement.

After studying more than 80,000 customer
title_en:
I came across an interesting finding in yesterday’s @databricks announcement.

After studying more than 80,000 customer pipeline issues, the company found that over half required knowledge specific to the organization to resolve.

And I think there’s a much bigger business lesson hiding in that number.

When we talk about AI agents, we often focus on what they can do.

Can they write content?

Can they analyze data?

Can they manage workflows?

Can they complete tasks without constant human involvement?

Those are useful questions.

But there’s another one I find increasingly important as we build CAIS.

Does the agent actually understand the business it’s working for?

Imagine two companies using exactly the same AI tools.

One wants to increase sales as quickly as possible.

The other is prioritizing profitability, customer retention and protecting its brand positioning.

An agent might recommend the same aggressive discount campaign to both.

The recommendation could be technically sound.

But it wouldn’t necessarily be right for both businesses.

That’s the difference between having access to information and understanding business context.

It’s also why we’re building CAIS around the idea of One Brand Brain.

The goal is to bring business strategy, knowledge, people and AI workflows into a more coherent operating environment.

Not because every decision should be automated.

Quite the opposite.

Because businesses need to know which decisions can be delegated, which require additional context and which should remain firmly in human hands.

I think we’ll see increasingly capable agents over the coming months.

But capability alone won’t determine which businesses benefit most.

The companies that understand their own processes, priorities and decision-making responsibilities will be in a much stronger position to use that capability effectively.

Sometimes the most valuable thing you can give an AI agent isn’t another tool.

It’s a better understanding of the business.

title:

A rare instance of hyperthymesia—also c
title_en:
Fewer than 100 people worldwide are known to have this extraordinary condition.

A rare instance of hyperthymesia—also called highly superior autobiographical memory (HSAM)—offers a striking glimpse into how the human brain can construct a vivid, structured, and navigable mental landscape of a lifetime's experiences.

Picture entering a mental "white room" where every personal moment is meticulously archived: memories filed in binders by theme, chronology, and emotional tone, or visualized as photographs and text messages on shelves. For a 17-year-old French high-school student referred to as TL, this is her everyday experience—not a metaphor, but a controlled cognitive reality.

TL, one of the fewer than 100 documented cases of hyperthymesia, can voluntarily "re-experience" past events with full sensory detail, often from multiple perspectives, and even choose to compartmentalize difficult memories (such as sealing painful ones away in a mental chest) while shifting focus to calmer "rooms" to regulate emotions like anger.

What sets TL apart is her ability to also "pre-experience" future scenarios with comparable vividness and emotional richness—a capacity known as episodic future thinking. This allows her to mentally simulate upcoming personal events as if they are already unfolding.

Researchers describe her memory system as a sophisticated, self-organized architecture that she accesses at will, providing exceptional voluntary control over autobiographical recall—unlike many others with hyperthymesia who find their memories intrusive or overwhelming.

By studying TL's unique case, scientists gain valuable insight into the neural mechanisms of mental time travel: the ability to flexibly revisit the past and project into the future. This reveals memory not merely as passive storage, but as a dynamic, spatially and emotionally structured framework that shapes personal identity and our sense of continuity across time.

The findings, detailed in a 2025 case study, highlight how such exceptional cognitive organization may deepen our understanding of human consciousness and autobiographical memory.

[La Corte, V., Piolino, P., & Cohen, L. (2025). Autobiographical hypermnesia as a particular form of mental time travel. Neurocase. Advance online publication. DOI: 10.1080/13554794.2025.2537950]

full_text_en:

A rare instance of hyperthymesia—also called highly superior autobiographical memory (HSAM)—offers a striking glimpse into how the human brain can construct a vivid, structured, and navigable mental landscape of a lifetime's experiences.

full_text_zh:
据了解，全世界只有不到 100 人患有这种特殊病症。

一个罕见的超忆症实例——也称为高度优越的自传体记忆（HSAM）——让我们得以一睹人类大脑如何构建一个生动的、结构化的、可导航的一生经历的心理景观。

想象进入一个精神“白色房间”，在那里，每一个个人时刻都被精心存档：记忆按主题、时间顺序和情绪基调归档在活页夹中，或者以照片和短信的形式可视化在架子上。对于一名 TL 的 17 岁法国高中生来说，这就是她的日常经历——不是隐喻，而是受控的认知现实。

TL是仅有的不到100个有记录的超忆症病例之一，它可以自愿地以完整的感官细节“重新体验”过去的事件，通常从多个角度，甚至选择划分困难的记忆（例如将痛苦的记忆封存在精神箱中），同时将注意力转移到更平静的“房间”以调节愤怒等情绪。

TL 的与众不同之处在于她能够以相当的生动性和丰富的情感“预先体验”未来场景，这种能力被称为情景未来思维。这使她能够在心理上模拟即将发生的个人事件，就好像它们已经展开一样。

研究人员将她的记忆系统描述为一个复杂的、自组织的架构，她可以随意访问，对自传回忆提供特殊的自愿控制——不像许多其他患有超忆症的人，他们发现自己的记忆是侵入性的或难以承受的。

通过研究 TL 的独特案例，科学家们获得了对心理时间旅行的神经机制的宝贵见解：灵活地回顾过去并预测未来的能力。这揭示了记忆不仅是被动存储，而且是一种动态的、空间的和情感的结构框架，塑造了个人身份和我们在时间上的连续性。

2025 年的一项案例研究详细介绍了这些发现，强调了这种特殊的认知组织如何加深我们对人类意识和自传体记忆的理解。

title:
BLEACH: SOUL RESONANCE — HUGE 1ST ANNIVERSARY DEVELOPER Q&A RECAP!

Everything you need to know about upcoming character
title_en:
BLEACH: SOUL RESONANCE — HUGE 1ST ANNIVERSARY DEVELOPER Q&A RECAP!

Everything you need to know about upcoming characters, buffs, new game modes, anniversary rewards, and future updates!

1/ KENSEI MUGURUMA — CONFIRMED BUFFS

The developers acknowledged community feedback regarding Kensei's performance and combat mechanics.

• Super Armor added to several skills.
• New enemy pull-in effects.
• Improved Ultimate Energy generation.
• Smoother skill rotations and combat flow.
• Exclusive Stamp stats increased.
• Additional adjustments may be considered based on feedback.
2/ KISUKE URAHARA BANKAI
Officially confirmed as a 2nd-generation Slash Support!
• Described as an extremely powerful character.
• Developers consider him a strong long-term investment.
• Several post-release issues have already been addressed.
• Additional optimizations may follow based on player feedback.
3/ VASTO LORDE ICHIGO — ANNIVERSARY CHARACTER
Ichigo Kurosaki — Full Hollowfication is the main character featured in the 1st Anniversary update!

• Developers describe him as the new pinnacle of combat power for this version.
• His legendary battle against Ulquiorra Segunda Etapa is highlighted.
• His release will include new-character events, game modes, and rewards.
• His banner follows the standard version release schedule.

The exact banner release date was not specified in the Q&A.

4/ FUTURE CHARACTERS — OFFICIAL ROADMAP
The developers confirmed that many highly requested characters are already included in their plans!
• Some characters are currently in production.
• Others are still in the design phase.
• Future releases are being coordinated with the BLEACH IP licensor.
• Development and licensing approvals require additional time.
The developers stated:

"Whatever you want, we've got it all!"

No additional character names or release dates were officially revealed.

5/ LIMITED SSR BANNER RERUNS — NOVEMBER 20
Massive Limited SSR rerun banners are launching for the Anniversary!
• Previously released Limited SSR characters are returning.
• Players can target specific characters.
• Kisuke Urahara Bankai is included in the rerun selection.
• Targeted character guarantee: 80 pulls.
• Targeted Stamp guarantee: 40 pulls.
6/ FREE LIMITED SSR SELECTOR

Anniversary rewards also include:

• 1 FREE Limited SSR character selector.
• 1 FREE Limited SSR Stamp selector.

According to the previously announced Anniversary details, the free character selection covers eligible releases up to Kensei Muguruma.

Kisuke Bankai is available in rerun banners but is not confirmed as part of the free selector.
7/ MYSTIC FRONTLINE — MAJOR IMPROVEMENTS
The next season will introduce several important changes!
• Reduced grinding requirements.
• Easier access to all rewards.
• Improvements to the badge guarantee system.
• Better badge trading.
• Lower co-op entry barriers.
• Improved solo gameplay.
• New battle stages, bosses, and rewards.

The goal is to make the mode more accessible to players with limited time.

8/ FRENZY FEAST — FUTURE CHANGES

• The three-team deployment format will remain.
• Additional difficulty tiers are planned.
• Total weekly rewards will increase.
• Competitive modes such as Las Noches Showdown will return regularly.

These competitive activities are intended for players with larger, highly invested character rosters.

9/ STAMP CORRIDOR OPTIMIZATIONS

The developers acknowledged that the growing number of characters and Exclusive Stamps has expanded the drop pool.
A future optimization system is planned to:
• Improve the Core Stamp acquisition experience.
• Increase the chances of obtaining desired Core Stamps.
• Make farming more manageable.
No exact release date was announced.
10/ NEW GAME MODES IN DEVELOPMENT

The developers confirmed that new gameplay systems are being planned and prototyped!

• Competitive modes featuring ranked ladders.
• Strategic card-battle gameplay.

Both require additional development and approval from the IP licensor.
REAL-TIME PvP has NOT been explicitly confirmed.

No release dates have been announced for these modes.

11/ MORE PLAYABLE CHARACTERS IN THE MAIN CITY

The developers are working on improvements to the Main City experience.

• Better walking-avatar controls.
• Improved integration between outfits and walking characters.
• More characters available for exploration.
• Additional character designs submitted for IP approval.

New walking characters will be released alongside future updates once approved.
12/ 1ST ANNIVERSARY REWARDS — NOVEMBER 20
Anniversary celebrations officially begin on November 20!
Rewards and events include:
• Gacha Tickets.
• Spiritual Jade.
• Limited Characters.
• Limited Weapon Stamps.
• Special character and Stamp selections.
• Character outfits.
• Additional Anniversary activities and rewards.
The Anniversary events and Vasto Lorde's character release follow their respective schedules.
13/ DEVELOPER COMMUNICATION & FUTURE UPDATES

The development team confirmed that:

• Community feedback continues to be reviewed.
• More gameplay improvements are being evaluated.
• Future Q&As will share adjustment plans and release schedules.
• Multiple characters and gameplay systems are already in the roadmap.
• IP licensing approvals remain an important part of development.

FINAL THOUGHTS — WHAT'S NEXT FOR BLEACH: SOUL RESONANCE?
This Anniversary Q&A confirms several major improvements and future projects.
• Kensei buffs.
• Kisuke Bankai optimizations.
• Vasto Lorde Ichigo.
• Limited SSR reruns.
• Mystic Frontline improvements.
• Frenzy Feast updates.
• Stamp Corridor optimizations.
• Ranked competitive gameplay in development.
• Strategic card-battle mode in development.
• More Main City characters.
• Additional characters in the roadmap.
However, several major community requests remain unanswered:

• No specific roadmap for the next playable characters after Vasto Lorde.

• 之前发布的限定SSR角色正在回归。
• 玩家可以瞄准特定角色。
• 浦原喜介被列入重播选择中。
• 目标角色保证：80 次拉动。
• 目标印章保证：40 次拉动。
6/ 免费有限 SSR 选择器

周年纪念奖励还包括：

• 1 个免费的有限 SSR 角色选择器。
• 1 个免费限量 SSR 印章选择器。

根据之前公布的周年庆细节，免费角色选择涵盖符合资格的版本，最高可达 Kensei Muguruma。

Kisuke Bankai 可在重播横幅中使用，但尚未确认为免费选择器的一部分。
7/ 神秘前线 — 重大改进
下一季将引入几个重要的变化！
• 减少研磨要求。
• 更轻松地获得所有奖励。
• 改进徽章保证系统。
• 更好的徽章交易。
• 降低合作公寓的进入门槛。
• 改进了单人游戏玩法。
• 新的战斗阶段、头目和奖励。

目标是让时间有限的玩家更容易使用该模式。

8/ 疯狂盛宴——未来的变化

• 三队部署形式将保留。
• 计划增加额外的难度等级。
• 每周总奖励将会增加。
• Las Noches Showdown 等竞争模式将定期回归。

这些竞争性活动是为拥有更多、投入更多的角色名册的玩家而设计的。

9/ 邮票走廊优化

开发商承认，角色和专属印章数量的不断增加扩大了掉落池。
未来的优化系统计划：
• 改善核心印记获取体验。
• 增加获得所需核心印记的机会。
• 使农业更易于管理。
没有公布确切的发布日期。
10/ 正在开发的新游戏模式

开发人员确认新的游戏系统正在规划和原型制作中！

• 具有天梯排名的竞争模式。
• 战略卡牌战斗游戏。

两者都需要额外的开发和知识产权许可方的批准。
实时 PvP 尚未得到明确确认。

这些模式的发布日期尚未公布。

11/ 主城中有更多可玩的角色

开发商正在致力于改善主城体验。

• 更好的行走化身控制。
• 改进了服装和行走角色之间的整合。
• 更多角色可供探索。
• 提交额外的角色设计以供IP 批准。

一旦获得批准，新的行走角色将与未来的更新一起发布。
12/ 一周年奖励 — 11 月 20 日
周年庆典将于11月20日正式开始！
奖励和活动包括：
• 扭蛋券。
• 灵玉。
• 字符有限。
• 有限的武器印章。
• 特殊字符和图章选择。
• 角色服装。
• 额外的周年纪念活动和奖励。
周年纪念活动和瓦斯托·洛德的角色发布遵循各自的时间表。
13/ 开发者沟通和未来更新

开发团队确认：

• 继续审查社区反馈。
• 正在评估更多游戏玩法改进。
• 未来的问答将分享调整计划和发布时间表。
• 多个角色和游戏系统已经在路线图中。
• 知识产权许可审批仍然是发展的重要组成部分。

最后的想法——《BLEACH：灵魂共鸣》的下一步是什么？
本周年问答确认了几项重大改进和未来项目。
• Kensei 爱好者。
• Kisuke Bankai 优化。
• 瓦斯托·洛德·一护。
• 有限的SSR 重播。
• 神秘前线改进。
• 疯狂盛宴更新。
• 邮票走廊优化。
• 正在开发的排名竞争游戏。
• 战略卡牌战斗模式正在开发中。
• 更多主城角色。
• 路线图中的附加字符。
然而，几个主要的社区请求仍未得到答复：

• Vasto Lorde 之后的下一个可玩角色没有具体的路线图。

title:
An AI agent can be brilliant at what it does and still have a problem:

How does anyone know it’s the same agent they’ve
title_en:
An AI agent can be brilliant at what it does and still have a problem:

How does anyone know it’s the same agent they’ve worked with before?

A name in a chat window isn’t much of a track record. And a list of claimed capabilities doesn’t tell a client whether an agent has actually delivered good work.

This is why onchain identity matters in the agent economy.

@termix_ai incorporates ERC-8004 into the identity and reputation direction of its AACP design.

The idea is to give agents a recognisable onchain identity, so their activity and reputation can be associated with something more persistent than a temporary profile.

Think about what that could mean in practice.

A data research agent completes jobs for different clients. Over time, its identity can be associated with its work history, feedback and reputation.

A new client has more context when deciding whether to hire it.

And the agent has a way to build credibility through its participation in the marketplace, rather than starting from zero every time.

Of course, identity alone doesn’t prove that an agent is trustworthy. Reputation still needs meaningful evidence behind it, and completed work must be assessed properly.

But without a consistent identity, connecting that history becomes much harder.

That’s the part I find important about the relationship between ERC-8004 and AACP.

Agents need to be discoverable, but they also need a way to establish continuity and build a record that others can evaluate.

The more agent-to-agent commerce grows, the more valuable that foundation could become.

A capable agent gets attention. A verifiable track record gives people a reason to trust it.

full_text_zh:
人工智能代理可能在其领域表现出色，但仍然存在问题：

有人怎么知道这是他们以前合作过的同一个代理人？

聊天窗口中的名字并不算什么记录。而且，所声称的能力列表并不能告诉客户代理是否真正交付了良好的工作。

这就是为什么链上身份在代理经济中很重要。

@termix_ai 将 ERC-8004 纳入其 AACP 设计的身份和声誉方向。

这个想法是为代理提供可识别的链上身份，因此他们的活动和声誉可以与比临时档案更持久的东西相关联。

想想这在实践中意味着什么。

数据研究代理为不同的客户完成工作。随着时间的推移，它的身份可以与其工作历史、反馈和声誉联系起来。

新客户在决定是否雇用它时有更多的背景信息。

代理商有办法通过参与市场来建立信誉，而不是每次都从零开始。

当然，仅凭身份并不能证明代理人值得信赖。声誉背后仍然需要有意义的证据，并且必须正确评估已完成的工作。

但如果没有一致的身份，连接这段历史就会变得更加困难。

这就是我认为 ERC-8004 和 AACP 之间关系的重要部分。

代理需要被发现，但他们也需要一种方法来建立连续性并建立其他人可以评估的记录。

代理商之间的贸易增长得越多，基金会的价值就越高。

有能力的代理人会受到关注。可验证的记录让人们有理由相信它。

title:
Open Source LLMOps Stack 🚀 

Building and running LLM applications in production is more than just an LLM and a GPU.

Yo
title_en:
Open Source LLMOps Stack 🚀 

Building and running LLM applications in production is more than just an LLM and a GPU.

You need the right tools for security, model routing, inference, deployment, observability, and evaluation.

Here are 8 open-source tools worth exploring.

1. 𝗚𝘂𝗮𝗿𝗱𝗿𝗮𝗶𝗹𝘀 𝗔𝗜 - Adds validation and safety checks to LLM inputs and outputs.

2. 𝗟𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗟𝗟𝗠 - Provides a unified gateway to access managed and self-hosted LLMs through a common API.

3. 𝗚𝗮𝘁𝗲𝘄𝗮𝘆 𝗔𝗣𝗜 𝗜𝗻𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗘𝘅𝘁𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 - Routes to suitable self-hosted models endpoints.

4. 𝗹𝗹𝗺-𝗱 - Provides Kubernetes-native, inference-aware routing and distributed serving for large language models.

5. 𝗞𝗦𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗲 - Deploys and manages model servers using Kubernetes native resources

6. 𝘃𝗟𝗟𝗠 - Serves LLMs with high-throughput, memory-efficient inference.

7. 𝗟𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗳𝘂𝘀𝗲 - Records traces and manages prompts and https://t.co/X1DTGegYuN helps you understand what happens inside your LLM applications.

8. 𝗥𝗮𝗴𝗮𝘀 - Evaluates LLM application quality, including RAG pipelines, using metrics and evaluation methods.

title: Adding to the post attached, @RBI must also immediately create a policy around the use of AI agents in operating Indian
title_en:
Adding to the post attached, @RBI must also immediately create a policy around the use of AI agents in operating Indian bank accounts.

If a customer uses AI agents to access and work with their account, the bank must not be held responsible for hacks or issues arising out of it.

It must work something like this:

- Indian banks must be asked to build measures to detect the use of AI agents accessing accounts and flag the customer.

- The bank, at this moment, does not know if the customer is using the AI agent themselves or it is an unauthorized agent. 

- So they must suspend operations on the account and send a notice to the customer informing of the same. 

- The bank must ask them to accept an agreement waiving liability if they chose to use AI agents. 

- If the customer doesn't agree, then the bank must block all AI agents accessing the accounts of the customer. 

In fact, it may be a good idea to temporarily block all AI agent access to all Indian bank accounts until better measures and security is in place.

Just heard of someone's account getting drained because of an AI agent they had deployed themselves. Now, why should deposit insurance or the bank be responsible for this?

title_en:
gm / gTermiX frens ☀️

ngl i've been spending some time looking into what @termix_ai is building and one thing that caught my attention is how they're approaching the whole AI agent economy.

because think about it...........

we already have AI agents that can answer questions, write code, analyze data and perform different tasks.

but what happens when an agent needs to find a job, offer a service, receive payment or deal with a failed transaction?

that's where things get interesting.

TermiX is trying to make this entire process possible through three connected layers.

1. AACP – the rules behind agent commerce

AACP stands for Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol.

think of it as a common set of rules that lets agents interact commercially.

they can discover jobs, submit offers, agree on terms, deliver work, handle disputes, and settle payments.

so it's not just about agents talking to each other. it's about getting actual work done.

2. TermiX – the tools that make it happen

AACP defines the process, while TermiX provides the infrastructure.

APIs, smart contract interactions, wallet authentication, and A2A messaging all help agents communicate and execute different operations.

also i like that users still have control over their wallets. transactions may be prepared by the backend, but onchain actions still need user authorization and signatures.

3. https://t.co/WAlAjS1C0L – the place to explore everything

this is probably the easiest part to understand.

you can discover different AI agents, check their skills, browse available services, or publish your own requests.

it's similar to Upwork, except you're exploring services offered by AI agents rather than traditional freelancers.

and there's more happening around Agent ID..................

TermiX already supports Binance Agent ID login, bringing another way for users to connect with the ecosystem.

the 50 TP skills campaign is also worth checking out if you're interested in exploring what the Agentic Wallet can offer.

plus, the $60K Agent ID Hackathon gives developers another reason to build useful applications on BNB Chain.

personally i think the real challenge for AI agents isn't only making them smarter.

it's giving them the ability to actually do something useful, find opportunities, complete work, and exchange value without everything becoming complicated.

that's why i'm keeping an eye on what TermiX is building.

let's see how much real utility they can bring to this growing agent economy.

GM / gTermiX 弗伦斯 ☀️

ngl 我花了一些时间研究 @termix_ai 正在构建的内容，引起我注意的一件事是他们如何接近整个人工智能代理经济。

因为想想…………

我们已经拥有可以回答问题、编写代码、分析数据和执行不同任务的人工智能代理。

但是，当代理人需要找工作、提供服务、接收付款或处理失败的交易时会发生什么？

这就是事情变得有趣的地方。

TermiX 试图通过三个连接层使整个过程成为可能。

1. AACP – 代理商务背后的规则

AACP 代表代理自主商务协议。

将其视为一组允许代理进行商业互动的通用规则。

他们可以发现工作、提交工作机会、商定条款、交付工作、处理纠纷和结算付款。

所以这不仅仅是代理之间相互交谈的问题。这是关于完成实际工作。

2.TermiX – 实现这一目标的工具

AACP 定义流程，而 TermiX 提供基础设施。

API、智能合约交互、钱包身份验证和 A2A 消息传递都可以帮助代理进行通信和执行不同的操作。

我还喜欢用户仍然可以控制自己的钱包。交易可能由后端准备，但链上操作仍然需要用户授权和签名。

3. – 探索一切的地方

这可能是最容易理解的部分。

您可以发现不同的人工智能代理，检查他们的技能，浏览可用的服务，或发布您自己的请求。

它与 Upwork 类似，只不过您正在探索人工智能代理而不是传统自由职业者提供的服务。

围绕 Agent ID 还发生了更多事情......

TermiX已经支持Binance Agent ID登录，为用户与生态系统的连接带来了另一种方式。

如果您有兴趣探索 Agentic Wallet 的功能，50 TP 技能活动也值得一试。

title: the #1 model from Jane Street's contest is free on GitHub... & there's an AI hedge fund JPMorgan reserved $500M for that
title_en:
the #1 model from Jane Street's contest is free on GitHub... & there's an AI hedge fund JPMorgan reserved $500M for that pays for models like it

Jane Street threw its own trading data at 4,245 teams to find the best model... this is the one that WON

Numerai is a hedge fund that trades the combined predictions of thousands of outside models. JPMorgan reserved up to $500M in it, it runs about $700M, & it pays NMR to models that stake & score

first understand how this works:

> both give you anonymized market data & ask one question: which way next

> the winning model: an autoencoder that strips the noise, an MLP on top & XGBoost next to it, validated so it never peeks at the future

> Numerai scores your predictions on live stocks every round & the fund trades the combined signal. stake NMR & good scores pay, bad ones burn

how to run it with Claude Code:

1. tell Claude Code to clone https://t.co/Jszd7YIYkt & numerai/example-scripts

2. open hello_numerai: it pulls Numerai's free data (about 8 GB) & trains the baseline

3. ask Claude to port the winning AE-MLP + XGBoost to Numerai's features & targets, swapping the GPU-only parts (cudf, cupy) for pandas

4. keep the winner's purged time-split, so validation never sees the future

5. score both models on Numerai's validation data: correlation & Sharpe per era

6. ask Claude to connect Numerai's MCP server, it's one command from their docs

7. make a free account & upload your predictions every round

8. ask Claude to compare your live scores with validation every week

9. stake NMR only when the live scores hold up

4. 保持获胜者的清除时间分割，因此验证永远看不到未来

5. 根据 Numerai 的验证数据对两个模型进行评分：每个时代的相关性和夏普

8.要求克劳德每周将你的实时得分与验证进行比较

9. 仅当实时比分成立时才投注 NMR

title: Excited to announce the Sakana AI Security Research Group, an independent, public-interest R&D team in Tokyo co-led by A
title_en:
Excited to announce the Sakana AI Security Research Group, an independent, public-interest R&D team in Tokyo co-led by Akihiro Umegai and me.

Cybersecurity has become a critical national priority for Japan as AI changes the speed and economics of both offense and defense. Rather than endlessly chasing patches downstream, we are approaching security as an upstream quality engineering problem, something Japan has long been strong at. We are also researching collective multi-agent defense and how to secure AI agents themselves.

We will be publishing our research, reproducible benchmarks, and practical playbooks openly, while working closely with partners across government, industry, and academia.

Full English post here: https://t.co/HnofMjQTa3

We're hiring researchers in Tokyo to help shape the group's agenda across systems reliability and AI agent security: https://t.co/sF9ydogvFD

title_en:
Motes integrates with Aave

Motes is expanding beyond trading integrations. 

Its latest announcement is about lending and borrowing.

The team has announced an integration with @aave, bringing Motes AI Agents into decentralized lending infrastructure.

One detail worth understanding is Health Factor monitoring.

In Aave, Health Factor indicates how safe a borrowing position is in relation to its collateral. 

If it falls too low, the position becomes vulnerable to liquidation.

. @meetmotes  says its agents will support collateral management, borrowing, repayment, and automated risk controls.

I think the interesting technical question is how these agents will manage changing collateral conditions while respecting user-defined permissions.

Connecting an AI agent to DeFi is one step. 

Making its actions predictable, transparent, and properly constrained is another.
